name: maypole

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The maypole is a folkloric object and custom. It was a fresh-cut sapling re-erected near the festivals of Beltane. The pole stood as a reminder of the life that springs up in woods and fields each spring. Dancers wrapped ribbons around the pole and performed elaborate, synchronized dances beneath it. Monaghan links the custom to Morris dancing. Some scholars see the maypole as a degraded form of the cosmic world tree.
objective: Document the maypole, the folkloric object and custom linked to the Beltane festivals.
key_results: Record the maypole as a strong straight sapling re-erected at Beltane.
Record the ribbon dance performed beneath it.
Record the link to Morris dancing.
Record the reading of the maypole as a degraded world tree.
